name: Ipulo-Olulu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Tuinstra, Anna. 2015. A phonological sketch of the Ipulo language. 121pp. (also Tuinstra 2017, Revising the Ipulo Orthography, phonology/tone)
earlier_scan.note: Full phonological sketch exists (SIL Cameroon/CanIL thesis) but PDF unreachable (sil.org 403, arcabc 410); tonal Tivoid, sketch likely addresses stress/tone

sources.citation: Tuinstra, Anna Grace. 2017. Revising the Ipulo Orthography: Linguistic analysis with an emphasis on tone marking. MA thesis, Graduate Institute of Applied Linguistics (Dallas). 259 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.3 (segments, syllables; max syllable CGVC) and Ch.4 (tone: 'Ipulo has two tones, high (H) and low (L)...', p.41, RTT analysis) contain no mention of stress or accent (only 'accent' = diacritic marks in orthography).

sources.citation: Tuinstra, Anna. 2019. Ipulo Phonology and Morphophonology. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 102 pp. (explicitly a corrective/update of Tuinstra 2015a 'A phonological sketch of the Ipulo language')
sources.note: Nothing. Full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/penult/intonation finds no statement. Sec. 5 Syllables (pp.15-17) and sec. 6 Tones (pp.18-40) describe a two-tone (H, L) system with LH, HL, H-downstep-H surface melodies, tone spread, downstep, contours; no word-stress or accent statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Tuinstra, Anna. 2018. Revised Ipulo Orthography Guide. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon (SIL Language and Culture Archives).
sources.note: Nothing; orthography guide with a tone chapter (sec. 3), no stress statement.
